inspection_summary: Verified the frozen SHA-256 and 1027-line count, then inspected every line. The article develops an RH-conditional Montgomery–Odlyzko gap criterion, motivates a polynomially weighted divisor-coefficient family, reduces its denominator and numerator to explicit nested integrals, and reports optimized polynomial witnesses. Prose and structural transitions are coherent; dense extracted formulas remain usable for planning but retain text-layer ordering and symbol-loss risk.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter, abstract, and contents
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the coefficient-sequence contribution and the improved normalized small- and large-gap bounds; otherwise bibliographic navigation.

sections_inspected.label: Background and coefficient design
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines normalized gap extremals, states the conditional theorem and threshold criterion, surveys coefficient improvements, introduces the paper's simplified prime-divisor perturbation, and records method limits.

sections_inspected.label: Reduction lemmas
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Provides an iterated-integral collapse and asymptotics converting divisor-weighted sums, including inserted prime divisors, into continuous integrals.

sections_inspected.label: Denominator expansion
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Splits the quadratic coefficient norm into base, cross, and second-order prime-divisor pieces and evaluates each as a scaled nested integral.

sections_inspected.label: Numerator expansion
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Decomposes the oscillatory numerator into four interaction classes and derives their main integral contributions via prime reduction, Mertens/Abel summation, divisor decompositions, and variable changes.

sections_inspected.label: Assembly, optimization, and back matter
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Reassembles the quotient, reports polynomial parameters found by Newton-type optimization for both gap directions, then gives acknowledgements and references.

accepted_units.title: Normalized zero gaps and the Montgomery–Odlyzko threshold criterion
accepted_units.why_material: Connects pair-correlation motivation, the conditional target bounds, and the functional h(c) whose crossing of 1 turns a coefficient choice into a large- or small-gap conclusion; it also records early coefficient choices and attained bounds.
accepted_units.context_note: Immutable v1 span; lines 75–87 are needed in v2 to recover the definitions and normalization of lambda and mu before the span begins.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on extracted displayed formulas for pair correlation, h(c), g_c, and the coefficient families; surrounding prose fixes their logical roles despite moderate symbol-order risk.

accepted_units.title: From divisor weights to Feng–Wu's prime-moment enrichment
accepted_units.why_material: Shows how successive coefficient designs enrich a basic divisor weight with shape polynomials and prime-factor moments, and identifies an equivalent one-prime power-sum representation whose calculations are simpler.
accepted_units.context_note: Overlaps the historical tail of u01 so the progression from the Conrey–Ghosh–Gonek family through Bui–Milinovich–Ng to Feng–Wu remains coherent.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The conceptual progression is explicit in prose, but exact coefficient equivalence is formula-dependent and should be checked against the page image before exact reuse.

accepted_units.title: Simplified coefficient perturbation and intrinsic threshold limits
accepted_units.why_material: Introduces the paper's base polynomial plus prime-divisor correction, explains the tradeoff between generality and explicit evaluability, and distinguishes coefficient optimization from known limits of the Montgomery–Odlyzko framework.
accepted_units.context_note: Immutable v1 span; lines 197–216 are needed to see precisely which Feng–Wu representation is being simplified.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on a multi-line coefficient formula with OCR ordering risk; the prose reliably establishes the simplification and the stated method limitations.

accepted_units.title: Collapsing multiplicative convolution and divisor sums to nested integrals
accepted_units.why_material: Lemma 1 collapses an iterated logarithmic convolution, while Lemma 2 supplies the asymptotic bridge from divisor-weighted sums, including multiple prime insertions, to continuous integrals used throughout the proof.
accepted_units.context_note: The source cites Feng and Wu for the proofs; this article uses the lemmas as reusable transformation rules rather than reproving them.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Highly formula-dependent; prose, displayed integration bounds, and the named constant A_r recover the intended transformations, but exact exponents and products need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Base and cross contributions to the coefficient norm
accepted_units.why_material: Expands the denominator of h(c), isolates its base and linear prime-correction terms, and shows how Lemma 2 plus scale-normalizing substitutions turn them into explicit polynomial integrals with controlled errors.
accepted_units.context_note: Immutable v1 span; the denominator decomposition is not complete without the quadratic prime-correction evaluation through line 484.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on dense extracted sums, integrals, and changes of variables; named pieces D-tilde_1 through D-tilde_3 and equation labels preserve the derivational structure.

accepted_units.title: Separating diagonal and distinct-prime effects in the quadratic correction
accepted_units.why_material: Splits the squared prime-divisor perturbation into a two-prime Möbius-weighted term and a same-prime term, then reduces both to explicit nested integrals; this completes the denominator needed for optimization.
accepted_units.context_note: Read with u03: it is the omitted final component of the denominator expansion rather than an independent argument.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The split and integral geometry are formula-dependent, with visible extraction ambiguity in limits and subscripts; exact numerical implementation requires page-image verification.

accepted_units.title: Prime reduction and sine-kernel integral for the unperturbed numerator
accepted_units.why_material: Defines and partitions the numerator, extracts the prime main contribution for N1, then uses Lemma 2, Mertens' theorem, Abel summation, order exchange, and scale variables to expose the sine-kernel integral governing the base interaction.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the full N1 route from the four-way algebraic expansion through equation (7), preserving why the final kernel appears.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Relies on formula layout for sums and integrals; the sequence of named transformations is textually explicit, while exact factors and error exponents require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Nested integral for a prime-divisor correction on one coefficient factor
accepted_units.why_material: Reparameterizes N2 by its prime variables, reuses the N1 inner-sum calculation, and applies the prime-sum asymptotic to produce a deeper nested integral coupling P1, the corrected polynomial, and the sine kernel.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the first numerator term induced by the added prime-divisor coefficient and is structurally compared with N1 in the source.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact variable nesting is displayed-formula dependent and moderately OCR-fragile; prose establishes the substitutions and reuse of equation (6).

accepted_units.title: Splitting whether the oscillatory prime enters the divisor correction
accepted_units.why_material: Uses the divisor-sum identity for pk to separate N3 into the inherited divisor contribution and the new contribution of p itself, yielding one N2-like integral and one N1-like integral before recombination.
accepted_units.context_note: The distinction between p already dividing k and p entering through pk is the conceptual source of the two terms.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on equation (9) and formula layout for N31 and N32; prose makes the combinatorial split recoverable, but exact coefficients need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Three interaction classes from corrections on both coefficient factors
accepted_units.why_material: Expands the two divisor-correction sums into shared-divisor, squared-new-prime, and mixed-new-prime classes N41, N42, and N43, and reduces each to a distinct nested integral contribution.
accepted_units.context_note: Completes the numerator hierarchy generated by the coefficient perturbation and supplies equations (11)–(13) used in final assembly.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: This is the most extraction-sensitive span: multi-level sums and integration limits are visible but crowded, so the three-way mechanism is usable while exact transcription requires page-image checking.

accepted_units.title: Assembling h(c) and optimizing explicit polynomial witnesses
accepted_units.why_material: Combines the derived denominator and numerator pieces, then records polynomial degrees, parameters, and coefficients whose computed threshold crossings yield the theorem's small- and large-gap bounds, including the Newton and relaxed-Newton search procedures.
accepted_units.context_note: The tables are compact computational certificates tied to the preceding asymptotic formulas; they are not an independent proof without those reductions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Table extraction is readable but alignment-sensitive; exact polynomial coefficients and the comparison of h(c) with 1 should be verified against the rendered table before reproduction.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Threshold functional as a bridge from coefficient design to gap bounds
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A conditional zero-gap problem is converted into finite-dimensional coefficient design by expressing both sides of h(c) as explicit integral functionals and searching for a crossing of the threshold 1.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The evidence is conditional on RH, tied to this Montgomery–Odlyzko functional and its asymptotics, and does not show that richer coefficients overcome the method's intrinsic range.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Prime-divisor enrichment creates a hierarchy of interaction integrals
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Adding a prime-divisor polynomial correction expands the quadratic and shifted products into systematically classifiable zero-, one-, and two-correction interactions, each reduced by the same sum-to-integral toolkit.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The extracted formulas support the interaction pattern more securely than exact constants, integration bounds, or exponents, which require scan verification.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Tractable reparameterization versus coefficient generality
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: An equivalent prime-power representation motivates a deliberately less general coefficient family whose payoff is explicit Montgomery–Odlyzko expressions and direct polynomial optimization.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The reported numerical improvement is slight and solver/procedure-specific; the source does not establish that the simplified family is optimal among the more general alternatives.
